compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional migration meeting, either person could bring a schedule, ask for a named owner or verify an acceptance condition. Those actions can reflect the requirements of the project.

Thinking and Judging describe shared preferences in the model. Neither code tells you who will meet a deadline or stop a release when a check fails.

The difference falls on E/I and S/N, and the axes are read separately. E/I says whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often; S/N says whether evidence trusts checkable fact and experience more, or notices links and possibility faster. The two cannot be merged into outward goals against inward experience: introversion does not mean indifference to an outward goal, and leaning N does not mean ignoring experience.

### ENTJ and ISTJ: four hours of window left, what cutting scope and completing the list each cost

In this fictional project, two people review the same four-hour cutover window. Three business areas are in scope, and two scheduled reports have no named owner. Both people have the same documentation and decision authority.

One way to read the documentation is to look for links between systems that could produce a wider disruption. Another is to verify which scheduled jobs are still running and which teams rely on the reports. Those approaches illustrate S/N. Both people can apply the same acceptance criteria and discuss which work fits the window.

Reducing scope can leave work for another window. Checking every item can leave too little time for acceptance. The trade-off depends on actual dependencies, risk and staffing.

Have both reviewers compare what might break if an item moves with what happens if it stays where it is. Then check those assumptions against the records. This tests the plan and cannot distinguish ENTJ from ISTJ.

Fi here means a theoretical preference for evaluating by inner value, and it is not used to infer where anyone's limits sit, still less how hard their line is, and least of all what they would actually do.

What gets swapped is the two perceiving positions: Ni and Se for Si and Ne. That is not one looking forward and one looking back. Ni and Si both process internally and take different material — the first takes trend and the key variable, the second existing practice and records; Se and Ne both perceive outward, one on the resources available now, one on how else this could go.

In both J types, the outward judging process is Te. It is dominant for the extraverted ENTJ and auxiliary for the introverted ISTJ, whose dominant process is Si. The positions describe the model and cannot establish a sequence of actions.

compare_blocks.body:
The three examples below are fictional. They illustrate ways of reading information and coordinating decisions. A real migration follows its own authorised procedures, and actual document replacement requirements come from the issuing office.

### ENTJ and ISTJ: which modules move on Friday night

A narrower scope may leave a business dependency unresolved. A longer review reduces the time available to complete the work. Either concern could change the plan.

Compare the same scope and dependency notes. Record which assumptions still need checking before the people authorised to decide agree what fits the window.

### ENTJ and ISTJ: second week after go-live, a colleague says it never used to be like this

In this fictional project, finance flags a change in the export two weeks after launch. Both reviewers have the same old and new samples. Either can see how the required column fits existing workflows or look for patterns suggesting which other reports may need review.

Either type can check the mapping or propose a temporary export. The choice depends on what finance needs and what the team can support.

compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
The first mismatch takes punctuality and delivery to a checkpoint as belonging to ISTJ alone. ENTJ will also stake a promise on a launch date and will also stop a release when a checkpoint fails; filing reliable under one type makes both judgements wrong.

The second reads insisting on completing the checks before release as conservative. In a migration, skipping one check usually costs more in rework than two extra hours; whether to check follows the cost of a miss and the scope of authority, not preference.

A request to keep a procedure may reflect a verified requirement. A request to change it may point to a problem the current procedure does not solve. Ask what evidence supports the request.

The fourth uses cutting scope first or completing the list first as the test. Those are two trade-offs under one constraint, and who takes which depends on authority, whether dependencies are known, and whether a missed migration or a delay costs more; the same person switching between two projects is common.

The fifth reads T as cold and J as rigid. T says the basis of judgement leans objective and consistent, J says an arrangement forms outward first; either type can look after how someone feels, and either can change a plan at short notice.

compare_blocks.body:
In the fictional table, both people have the same system, data, time window, constraints and decision authority. They can use either approach. The labels distinguish ways of reading the information from the direction of attention.

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional migration meeting, either person could bring a schedule, ask for a named owner or verify an acceptance condition. Those actions can reflect the requirements of the project.

Thinking and Judging describe shared preferences in the model. Neither code tells you who will meet a deadline or stop a release when a check fails.

The difference falls on E/I and S/N, and the axes are read separately. E/I says whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often; S/N says whether evidence trusts checkable fact and experience more, or notices links and possibility faster. The two cannot be merged into outward goals against inward experience: introversion does not mean indifference to an outward goal, and leaning N does not mean ignoring experience.

### ENTJ and ISTJ: four hours of window left, what cutting scope and completing the list each cost

In this fictional project, two people review the same four-hour cutover window. Three business areas are in scope, and two scheduled reports have no named owner. Both people have the same documentation and decision authority.

One way to read the documentation is to look for links between systems that could produce a wider disruption. Another is to verify which scheduled jobs are still running and which teams rely on the reports. Those approaches illustrate S/N. Both people can apply the same acceptance criteria and discuss which work fits the window.

Reducing scope can leave work for another window. Checking every item can leave too little time for acceptance. The trade-off depends on actual dependencies, risk and staffing.

Have both reviewers compare what might break if an item moves with what happens if it stays where it is. Then check those assumptions against the records. This tests the plan and cannot distinguish ENTJ from ISTJ.

### ENTJ and ISTJ: why two functions are shared while a whole perceiving axis is swapped

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and ISTJ is Si–Te–Fi–Ne. What is shared is Te and Fi, but they weigh differently in the stack: Te is dominant for ENTJ and auxiliary for ISTJ; Fi is inferior for ENTJ and third for ISTJ. Fi here means a theoretical preference for evaluating by inner value, and it is not used to infer where anyone's limits sit, still less how hard their line is, and least of all what they would actually do.

What gets swapped is the two perceiving positions: Ni and Se for Si and Ne. That is not one looking forward and one looking back. Ni and Si both process internally and take different material — the first takes trend and the key variable, the second existing practice and records; Se and Ne both perceive outward, one on the resources available now, one on how else this could go.

In both J types, the outward judging process is Te. It is dominant for the extraverted ENTJ and auxiliary for the introverted ISTJ, whose dominant process is Si. The positions describe the model and cannot establish a sequence of actions.

In the Foundation’s overview, the third process is Sensing for ENTJ and Feeling for ISTJ, with either attitude shown as an option. This page uses Se for ENTJ and Fi for ISTJ. Those choices do not change the dominant or auxiliary process. See the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and [ISTJ profile](/en/personality/istj).

Either type can check the mapping or propose a temporary export. The choice depends on what finance needs and what the team can support.
